answers.core:
A text editor should be able to open the same script multiple times.
If it were just an add-on, people would still not know what they're missing.

That's a problem with editors in general.
People can not know they're missing a feature they didn't even know existed.

It's easy to ignore the ability to open the same file multiple times,
because theoretically it's not required at all,
but practically it makes a huge difference.

There is no faster way of jumping around in between different spots in a file,
than just by switching to the tab that's already there.

Again, I'm sorry for my rambling.

Thank you.
answers.workaround:
I've looked into that. It looks possible.
Regardless, I'd have to learn how, unlike you, who don't.

I'd be only doing it for myself, with no benefit to anyone else.

Trying to make it for the benefit of everyone would turn it into a whole project,
with considerations and decisions to make, distracting from my own project.

If I started this, I'd also be faced with the fact that it would get integrated into the main editor eventually,
(because it should be a default feature!), which means you'd have to rewrite a lot of it anyway.

Being able to open multiple scripts at the same time should be a *default* feature for a text editor.

Alternatively I could launch the editor twice, or even thrice, but ...
- that's not just a waste of RAM,
- it also messes with the ALT+TAB chain,
- meaning that reaching the browser window gets a lot more annoying,
- which would cause me to switch to "Virtual Desktops" ... 

... yeah, this isn't really a good option.

I'm sorry for all the rambling.

Thank you.

title: Allow opening the same script multiple times in the editor
